subject: k-pop fans
one_liner: Annex rents workspace to K-pop fans whose group chats now require six desks and a staffed mailroom.
brand_voice_notes: Use the straight-faced language of office leasing: desks, visitors, deliveries, occupied space. Let ordinary fan habits explain how someone ends up renting an office. Explain collectible photo cards and new-release viewing through actions. Fictional members have believable fan activities and day jobs. The frozen anti-ai-slop skill has been applied and the copy scanned. Compared with the recent K-pop entry, the humor comes from physical space filling up, room allowances running out and visitors arriving at reception.
demo_screen_concept: One workspace-booking screen shows Annex's furnished floor plan, a date selector and three options: Day pass, Resident and Private office. A persistent notice says 'Demo booking. No payment.' Initially, Day pass is selected. Clicking an available desk highlights it and shows the $32 day rate, access hours, 30 included screening-room minutes and two guest passes. Add a 45-minute screening-room reservation for a new music video: the inspector shows 30 minutes included and 15 extra minutes at $8, bringing the total to $40. Confirming changes the desk to occupied and displays a booking receipt with the same desk, room time and total. Selecting another plan previews its actual monthly price and allowances without confirming a purchase. A mailroom on the map shows why the Resident plan includes storage; clicking it reveals a sample delivery of 24 albums awaiting collection. The private office shows six individual desk-and-chair workstations, matching its six desks and six member keys. The numbered D01–D06 controls select desks in the separate shared area.

hero.h1: Your group chat has taken a lease.
hero.sub: Annex rents workspace to K-pop fans. Book a desk, reserve a room for the new video and send 96 copies of the same album to reception.

features.title: The room is booked for one video.
features.blurb: Reserve a screening room for a new music video. Every replay uses more of your included room time. The song is three minutes long; your reservation now runs until lunch.

features.title: Reception signed for all 96 copies.
features.blurb: Send bulk album orders to our staffed mailroom. Open them for the collectible photo cards inside, then put the spare albums on your rented shelf. Reception would like its trolley back.

features.title: Your card trade has visitors.
features.blurb: Issue a guest pass to someone bringing the photo card you're missing. Each additional trader needs a separate pass. A quick swap at your desk now involves five people waiting for you downstairs.

pricing_tiers.name: Day pass
pricing_tiers.tagline: You only need somewhere for today.
perks: One available desk from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.
30 minutes in a screening room; additional time costs $8 per 15 minutes.
Two guest passes for photo-card trades at your desk.
Take your albums home at closing.

pricing_tiers.name: Resident
pricing_tiers.tagline: The albums have somewhere to stay.
perks: A dedicated desk with access seven days a week.
Two screening-room hours each month; additional time costs $8 per 15 minutes.
Reception accepts up to 20 parcels a month; one storage shelf holds the albums you're still finding homes for.
Ten guest passes each month for traders and group-order pickups.

pricing_tiers.name: Private office
pricing_tiers.tagline: Give the fan club a door.
perks: A lockable office with six desks and six member keys.
Twelve screening-room hours each month; additional time costs $8 per 15 minutes.
Reception accepts up to 100 parcels a month; six storage shelves keep the corridor clear.
Fifty guest passes each month. Reception checks visitors against your pickup list.

observations.behavior: Fans replay a new music video to watch individual performers and compare reactions.
observations.mechanic: Book a physical screening room using a finite monthly allowance, then pay for extensions.
observations.consequence: A three-minute release occupies a room until lunch and becomes a recurring calendar reservation.

observations.behavior: Group-order organisers receive many copies of an album while collectors open copies for the photo cards inside.
observations.mechanic: Use a staffed mailroom and rent storage shelves alongside a dedicated desk.
observations.consequence: The office receives enough albums to recognise a member before their first visit, and storage becomes a reason to renew.

observations.behavior: Collectors arrange quick photo-card swaps that attract additional traders and friends.
observations.mechanic: Register each visitor, issue guest passes and meet arrivals at reception.
observations.consequence: A lunchtime swap produces a reception queue and consumes the collector's entire break.

source_product_patterns: Book an available desk on a workspace floor plan.
Choose between daily access, a dedicated desk and a private office.
Reserve shared rooms using included hours and paid extensions.
Receive deliveries at a staffed reception desk.
Assign storage space to a recurring membership.
Register visitors and issue a limited number of guest passes.
editorial_plan.composition_plan: The primary action is choosing a desk and confirming a demo reservation. Open with the Annex name, headline, short explanation and CTA, followed immediately by a wide booking preview with a readable floor plan and reservation inspector. Use architectural blue lines, graphite text and pale yellow occupied areas. Artwork one is an overhead furnished office drawing used inside the booking preview: desks, screening room and mailroom explain the rentable spaces, while live labels carry availability and prices. Artwork two is a mailroom shelf cutaway showing opened albums, removed photo cards and copies awaiting pickup; it explains why storage becomes a monthly expense. Below, give each feature an open passage with its relevant entitlement, then testimonials and a joined rental comparison. On mobile, place booking details below the map. The physical office setting develops a different mechanism from the recent K-pop voting rooms, and the rental prices replace the digest's recurring $19/$79 subscription ladder.

design_direction.style: Architectural leasing modernism: paper-white plans, graphite geometric headings, drafting-blue room boundaries and pale yellow occupancy fields. A furnished workspace prospectus with generous quiet margins.

fonts.pairing: Geometric Modern from bundled ui-ux-pro-max typography.csv

design_direction.archetype: Real-Time / Operations Landing from the bundled library: proposition and furnished booking preview, open service passages, member evidence and joined rental comparison.
design_direction.motion_vocab: 180ms color response on selection and buttons; no ambient motion. Reduced motion disables transitions.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Left-aligned headline with a compact proposition and primary booking action, followed immediately by a wide furnished floor plan and live reservation inspector. Mailroom cutaway supports storage explanation. Pale yellow is reserved for occupied space and the rental band.
design_direction.design_review: Compared all seven host digest identities. No matching style/palette/fonts tuple. Retained architectural product preview from approved brief; rejected library luxury Cinzel and teal because they suggest premium apartments and repeat recent mint. Geometric Modern Outfit/Work Sans is the bundled pairing. Door swing and adjoining occupied rooms differ from lifting straps, huddles, seeds, parcel tabs, lightsticks and film frames. Lower layout uses open passages rather than tiled features.

brand_kit.identity_rationale: An open doorway adjoining a second room expresses a fan activity acquiring extra floor space. Drafting lines and pale yellow occupied rooms belong to physical leasing, distinct from the recent fan-club lightstick identity.

logo.concept: Selected Gemini direction A: two adjoining blue floor-plan rooms with one yellow occupied space and a black door-swing detail, beside exact Annex lettering. B rejected: thinner offset wall planes read less clearly at icon size.
logo.clear_space: At least half the symbol height on every side
logo.placement: Landing navigation and footer; demo chrome; symbol favicon on both pages

graphic_language.medium: Axonometric architectural editorial illustration with blue linework, paper-white furniture, pale yellow occupied zones and restrained intentional typography.
graphic_language.motif: An adjoining room, open doorway and occupied floor area; thin drafting lines used at spatial boundaries.

graphic_language.texture: Subtle pencil and drafting-paper tooth inside artwork; flat CSS surfaces.

graphic_plan.purpose: Designed cutaway of opened album orders, collectible cards and storage shelves explains why albums occupy paid space.

images.rationale: Reserve calls for two original logo directions and two composed illustrations. No photography needed: physical space and album accumulation are best explained through furnished architectural drawings.

items.prompt: Design the actual finished original brand logo for "Annex", a fictional coworking office for K-pop fans whose album orders and viewing parties now require rented space. Direction A: architectural adjoining-room symbol with a precise open doorway / door-swing detail; compact floor-plan silhouette containing one pale yellow occupied room. Bespoke confident geometric sans wordmark exactly "Annex" to its right. Drafting blue #285DB5 and graphite #252E36 with pale yellow #F2DA7E, on completely flat paper-white #F7F8F4. Make the symbol distinct and legible at 32px, thick enough lines. Clean flat graphic design, no presentation board, no mockup, no gradients, no shadow, no extra text, no trademark copies. Horizontal lockup centered with ample clear space, symbol isolated to left of wordmark. 3:2 image.
items.verdict: Direction A selected. Exact Annex spelling, balanced bold lettering and compact floor-plan silhouette. Cropped only outer blank margin; no redesigned geometry. Stronger than B at small size; thick perimeter remains legible.

items.transformation: Exact accepted pixels: suppress pale background and yellow fill, recolor dark mark and lettering graphite, retain antialiased alpha.

items.verdict: Faithful outline and lettering; readable on paper-white.

items.transformation: Crop accepted symbol, center with clear space on paper-white square, resize to 128px.

items.verdict: Thick blue room boundaries remain recognizable at 24 and 32 pixels.

items.prompt: Approved identity reference attached: preserve its blue architectural geometry and yellow occupied-area language. Design an editorial architectural composition, an overhead furnished office plan for Annex coworking space for K-pop fans. Rectangular footprint with generous white corridors: left open desk area with two paired bench tables and six chairs; upper right a screening room with projector, screen and four chairs; lower right a mailroom with shelves of albums, a trolley and reception counter. A small six-person private office along top. Architectural blue #285DB5 linework, graphite #252E36 detail, pale yellow #F2DA7E occupied room floors, paper-white #F7F8F4. Beautiful restrained axonometric furniture, precision line weights, sophisticated architectural prospectus composition, human-scale details like headphones, photocard binder and album stacks. Compose only these exact large readable labels: "Desks", "Screening room", "Mailroom", "Private office". No desk numbers, prices, other text or watermarks. No rendered software UI. Leave margins and preserve whole outer footprint. A complete designed architectural artwork, not a plain flowchart or photograph. Wide landscape 3:2.
items.placement: Landing booking preview and demo floor plan, with the same six-workstation private-office HTML/SVG fitout on both pages
items.verdict: The source illustration has four room labels and the accepted blue/yellow identity. Its private office contains two workstations. Both HTML pages correct that room with an identical responsive SVG layer, reusing six desk-and-chair crops from this same asset, retaining the surrounding rooms and adding a live six-desk/six-key caption. No asset pixels were modified. Numbered desk controls refer to the separate shared area.
items.export: Full composition preserved; deterministic RGB WebP conversion, no crop.

items.prompt: Approved identity reference attached: use its exact geometric blue architectural language. Create a composed information-design artwork for Annex, an office rented by K-pop fans. Axonometric cutaway mailroom cabinet and trolley, with one opened shipping carton, neatly repeating album copies arranged upright on shelves, and a small collectible portrait card removed from one album. The point: many copies are opened for collectible cards, spare albums take up rented storage. Beautiful architectural sectional illustration, deliberate asymmetric layout with 3 large textual anchors integrated into drawing, rich furniture detail and bold graphic negative space. Exact text ONLY: "24 albums", "Photo cards kept", "Shelf space used". Give 24 album spines in four groups of six, with one visibly opened album; a few tiny illustrated portrait cards above the shelf. Do not label the number of photo cards. Drafting blue #285DB5, pale yellow #F2DA7E, graphite #252E36, paper-white #F7F8F4. Blue linework, restrained pencil texture. Typography must be large and legible. No extra copy, watermarks, logos, software UI or photography. Full uncropped composition, landscape 3:2.
items.placement: Landing mailroom passage and demo delivery details
items.verdict: Accepted: all three supplied labels spelled correctly, architectural cutaway and card extraction communicate why storage is rented. 24 is the sample delivery size; shelves are illustrative, not a literal spine-count chart. Large typography remains legible at mobile display size.
items.export: Full composition preserved; deterministic RGB WebP conversion, no crop.

discarded.prompt: Create the finished original logo for "Annex", coworking space for K-pop fans acquiring more rooms for their albums. Direction B, distinct from door-swing floor plans: two offset architectural wall planes with one projecting yellow shelf/room extension, forming a compact recognizable spatial symbol beside custom geometric sans lettering exactly "Annex". The visual idea is a building adding an annex, not an initial in a box. Drafting blue #285DB5, graphite #252E36, pale yellow #F2DA7E, flat paper-white #F7F8F4 background. Confident well-kerned typography. Flat actual logo only, horizontal lockup, generous clear space, no presentation board, no additional text, no shadow, no trademark copies.
discarded.verdict: Direction B is correctly spelled and attractive, but thinner offset wall planes and projecting shelf become ambiguous at favicon scale. A better communicates occupied adjoining rooms. Raw removed after comparison.
